title: MIG capacity affinity heuristics + cross-model kernel selector for H100/L40S/A10
creator: Leah Chen
description: Goal: improve steady-state throughput and tail latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads across H100, L40S and A10 by: 1) defining a compact heuristic that picks between multiple compiled kernel variants at request time (int8/qat/float), 2) affinitizing requests to MIG partitions or whole-GPU pools based on sequence-length distribution and power/clock headroom, and 3) co-scheduling prefill and decode stages to avoid pathological KV-cache thrash. We expect a 15-40% throughput uplift for common chat workloads and a reduction in p99 token latency by 10-25% depending on hardware.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: scoped as ephemeral policy + runtime change. Agreed to prioritize H100 + L40S experiments first, then validate A10. PM notes to include cost delta in release notes. (Leah)

2026-03-03 - Experiment plan posted: microbench harness (bash + pybench) that runs kernel matrix for seq_len=[8,32,128,512], batch=[1,4,16], kv-hit ratios, and service-like prefill/decode mixes. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/runtime/mig-affinity-bench (internal). (Asha)
2026-03-05 - Infra: reserved a small H100 pod (4x) and L40S pool (8x) in staging. Hooked perf counters and nvml telemetry. (Omar)

2026-03-07 - Early results: H100: best kernel variant shifts to precompute-gemm-fused variant for seq>=128 leading to 1.35x tokens/sec, L40S: smaller improvement ~1.18x. Observed KV eviction spikes when prefill+decode share same MIG slice. (Asha)

2026-03-09 - Design decision: implement two-layer selector: (A) fast cost-model (latency + token-cost estimate) computed from telemetry and lookup table, evaluated in runtime hotpath; (B) asynchronous profiler that updates the LUT periodically per model+seq histogram. Chosen to avoid branching in critical loop. (Leah)
2026-03-10 - PR opened for selector prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6123. Includes fallback to default kernel and telemetry tags for chosen kernel. (Asha)

2026-03-12 - Observability: added dashboard tile for kernel-choice distribution, per-MIG partition p99 token latency, and spill-over alerts. Early staging dash: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/bench/mig-affinity (internal). Next: validate on A10 and run long-lived soak for 48h. (Miguel)
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark harness reproducible and checked in under runtime/bench/mig-affinity
Selector reduces average per-token cost or improves p99 latency on H100 and L40S for at least 2 representative chat workloads (measured in staging)
No customer-facing error regression; rollout gated by automated canary and rollback if p99 increases >10%
Telemetry: kernel_choice, mig_partition, prefill_kv_hit_rate emitted and visible on release dashboards
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect kernel choice may increase latency for short-sequence requests. Mitigation: fast-path rule that forces low-latency kernel for seq<=16 and batch=1.

Risk: MIG fragmentation causing headroom oscillation between workloads. Mitigation: prefer whole-GPU for sustained high-throughput model classes; implement cooldown windows for partition reassignments.
Risk: unexpected thermal/clock throttling under new affinity policy. Mitigation: run thermal soak on H100/L40S and add nvml-driven clock-floor guardrails before full rollout.
implementation_notes: Add runtime hook in request router to call kernel_selector(model_id, seq_len, batch, kv_hit_est) -> kernel_variant_id
Selector LUT keyed by (model_family, seq_bucket, batch_bucket, hw_class, mig_size) with last_profiler_ts and weight decay
Profiler job: low-impact async microbench that samples requests and runs 1-2 trial kernels per model variant to update expected tokens/s and p99 projections
MIG affinity policy: compute score = util_est * headroom_factor - kv_eviction_penalty; threshold to pick dedicated partition vs whole GPU
Instrumentation: tag traces with kernel_variant and mig_affinity_decision, increment metrics runtime.kernel.choice and runtime.mig.selection
Rollout: canary on 5% of requests for 48h, compare against control for p50/p95/p99 and cost delta, then 25% for 24h, then 100% if no regressions
